title: SLO-driven amber routing and automated fallback throttle playbook for Dedicated/Private
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Private and Dedicated control planes occasionally exhibit partial degradation (increased p50/p90 latency, sporadic KV cache misses, or intermittent scheduling delays) that does not require a full region failover but does require targeted, short-lived traffic shaping.

This ticket defines an operational and implementation playbook for an "amber" routing tier: a controlled, SLO-driven intermediate state between green (normal) and red (full failover). Goals: (1) minimize user-visible errors during transient control-plane pressure, (2) avoid wholesale region swaps where possible, (3) provide deterministic fallback throttles and lightweight circuit breakers scoped per-customer or per-pool, and (4) make the system auditable and reversible.
acceptance_criteria: Amber routing state defined in control plane with explicit SLO thresholds and hysteresis
Automated policy engine can transition traffic to amber based on latency/error SLO signals without manual intervention
Per-pool and per-customer fallback throttle policies implemented and configurable (burst, sustained windows, retry-backoff)
Circuit-breaker taxonomy published and enforced (soft degrade, hard isolate) with audit logs
Runbook and playbook documented in Confluence with step-by-step remediation and rollback steps
End-to-end integration test that simulates a partial control-plane resource exhaustion and validates amber->green transition and amber->red escalation
Dashboard panels and alerts added to Console for amber transitions, per-customer throttle events, and policy overrides
tasks: Draft amber routing SLO definitions and hysteresis (PM + SRE) — complete first draft
Implement policy engine hooks in routing service to accept amber weight modifiers
Add throttle enforcement layer in tenant-admission-controller with per-window counters
Create circuit-breaker library shared by Dedicated controlplane and Private agent
Add audit logging for policy transitions and overrides to compliance log stream
Author Confluence playbook and runbook (initial + runbook validation checklist)
Write integration test harness that replays high-latency trace samples and KV cache miss patterns
Add Console dashboards and alert rules; add documentation link to incident pager runbook
notes: Trade-offs considered: aggressive per-tenant throttling reduces overall impact but risks customer SLA violations — mitigated by slow-start backoff and opt-out flags for enterprise customers
We chose hysteresis windows of 60s (enter amber) and 300s (exit amber) as initial values based on production experiments; these are configurable
KV cache warming: amber flows will prefer cache-warmed replicas via affinity hints. Implementation requires minor routing metadata extension
Security: policy transitions are privileged operations. We will require KMS-signed tokens for automated transitions in Private installs; security review slated
Rollback: any amber policy change can be rolled back via the control plane CLI and an automated 'force-green' flag will bypass throttles for 30s for emergency debugging

implementation_notes: Policy engine will expose a safe subset of controls to Console with an 'apply_preview' mode that evaluates without committing
Throttle enforcement must be idempotent across retries — use monotonic counters persisted in the per-tenant namespace

Ensure runbook includes escalation matrix (SRE on-call -> routing-service owner -> Eng manager) and an explicit metric to opt for full failover
